_comment: Example watchlist for poller.sh / pr-watch-poller.sh. Copy to $HOME/.config/run-issues/watchlist.json and replace every <placeholder>. Lookup order: RUN_ISSUES_WATCHLIST if set (and then it is the ONLY candidate — a missing file is an error, never a fallback), else $HOME/.config/run-issues/watchlist.json, else the legacy $HOME/dotfiles/machine-studio/run-issues-watchlist.json. JSON has no comment syntax — the _comment key is the convention used instead. LABEL SEMANTICS: `labels` (per repo, falling back to `default_labels`) are ANDed — an issue must carry EVERY listed label to be picked up. Listing `auto-clean`, `waiting` or `wip` here silently disables pickup for that repo: the pick query already excludes all three, so requiring one of them yields zero matches forever, with no error and no log line. See README section 6.2. OPTIONAL KEY `pr_watch_max_concurrent` (number, top-level): a separate concurrency cap for pr-watch-poller.sh only; when omitted it falls back to global_max_concurrent, so leaving it out keeps the current behaviour exactly. Because PR scans are seconds of work (unlike the tens-of-minutes orchestrator runs), raising it lets the PR watcher reach the whole watchlist faster without widening poller.sh's orchestrator concurrency. The env var PR_WATCH_GLOBAL_MAX overrides it. See CLAUDE.md section 7. OPTIONAL KEY `assignees` (array of GitHub logins, per repo): when present, only issues routed to one of those logins are picked up; when absent — the default — assignees are not looked at and pickup is exactly as it was. It is ANDed with `labels`, never a replacement for them. An issue qualifies if any of its assignees is on the list, OR, when it has no assignee at all, if its AUTHOR is on the list — so a hand-written issue runs without anyone assigning it, and the assignee field is the override that moves work to another machine. The flip side is a deliberate human opt-out: assigning an issue to a login OUTSIDE the list keeps it out of pickup even if a listed login opened it. An empty array means the same as no key: no assignee filtering. This is the second routing axis — labels are ANDed, so splitting work by label needs one label per machine, while assignees name the machine in GitHub's own UI. See README section 6.2.

repos._comment: Multi-remote form: one clone polling two orgs. Both labels are required on the issue (AND), so this entry picks up only issues carrying BOTH auto-run and backend — narrow the scope, never widen it.
Assignee-routed form: this host takes only issues assigned to <machine-user>, plus unassigned issues opened by <you>. Omit the key entirely to keep the label-only behaviour of the entries above.
